Class TextLabel

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.core.AbstractPanelElement<TextLabel>
com.trevlar.menukit.core.TextLabel
All Implemented Interfaces:
PanelElement
public class TextLabel extends AbstractPanelElement<TextLabel>
A non-interactive text label within a Panel. Renders text at a fixed position using drawString.

Two forms for the text content:

  • Fixed text — pass a Component directly.
  • Supplier-driven text — pass a Supplier<Component> for text that changes over time (dynamic values, state reflections, etc.).

ARGB color requirement (26.2): Colors must include an explicit alpha byte (e.g., 0xFF404040, not 0x404040). GuiGraphicsExtractor.text() silently discards text when ARGB.alpha(color) == 0. All color constants in this class use the 0xFF prefix. Consumer code passing custom colors must do the same.

Dynamic-width limitation with supplier text

TextLabel's width is derived from the rendered text's width. Auto-sizing elements with supplier-based variable content cannot guarantee layout stability — if the supplier returns different-length text each frame, the element's width changes per frame but panel layout is not re-resolved per frame. Consumers needing stable layout should use fixed-content variants or ensure the supplier returns same-width content across all evaluations (e.g., "Mode: AUTO" vs "Mode: MANUAL" where both render to similar widths).

Render-only; PanelElement.mouseClicked(double, double, int) inherits the default no-op behavior.

Construction — prefer spec(Component) / .at(x,y)

The positional constructors take childX/childY as their leading arguments. The fluent path keeps the position out of the argument list: use spec(Component) (or spec(int, int, Supplier) for supplier-driven text) to drop a label into a Row/Column layout, or construct without a position and call .at(x, y). The positional constructors remain for the cases where threading (x, y) through the constructor is the clearest spelling; they are not deprecated, just no longer the only path.

    • spec

      public static ElementSpec spec(net.minecraft.network.chat.Component text)
      Returns an ElementSpec for static text. Width inferred from font metrics at spec construction (single-shot evaluation of text.getString() via font.width(text)); height is font.lineHeight.

      Static text only. For supplier-driven dynamic text, use the explicit-dimension overload spec(int, int, Supplier) — supplier values can vary frame-to-frame and auto-inferred width from a single supplier evaluation would freeze layout against a stale snapshot.

    • setWrapWidth

      public void setWrapWidth(int wrapWidth)
      Sets the maximum horizontal pixel width this label may occupy. Zero (the default) disables wrapping — the label renders on a single line sized to its natural text width.

      When non-zero, the label switches to multi-line mode: getHeight() returns lineCount × font.lineHeight based on font.split(text, wrapWidth), and render(RenderContext) draws each wrapped line at successive vertical offsets.

      Called by the owning Panel's configuration pass when the Panel has a pinnedWidth (Phase 16g auto-wrap trigger). Consumers don't typically call this directly — set pinnedWidth on the Panel and the propagation runs automatically.

      Dynamic-supplier caveat: with supplier-driven text, font.split is re-evaluated each frame. If the supplier returns different-length text per frame, the wrapped line count (and thus panel height) can fluctuate. Same stability caveat documented on the class javadoc applies here.

      Parameters:
      wrapWidth - horizontal pixel budget for wrapped lines, or 0 to disable wrapping.

    • scale

      public TextLabel scale(float scale)
      Sets a uniform render scale (folded from the former MKHudText). The text is drawn through a GUI pose-matrix scale, and getWidth()/ getHeight()/naturalWidth() report the SCALED extent so the owning Panel reserves the right space. 1.0f (the default) skips the matrix entirely — the unscaled path is unchanged. Composes with wrap: wrapWidth stays a font-space number, the scale is applied only at the screen-pixel boundary.

      Must be > 0. A non-positive value is floored to a tiny positive minimum rather than allowed to produce a degenerate (zero / mirrored) render matrix — hardening the gap the former MKHudText left open.

      Returns:
      this label, for chaining

    • extraWrapHeight

      public int extraWrapHeight()
      Extra vertical pixels this label occupies BEYOND a single line because it wrapped — i.e. (lineCount - 1) × lineHeight, or 0 when not wrapped. The owning Panel uses this to reflow the elements below a wrapped label downward by exactly this amount, so a label that grows from one line to two doesn't paint over the next element (fixed-childY layouts stay overlap-free under auto-wrap).

    • naturalWidth

      public int naturalWidth()
      Natural width = the text's single-line rendered width. The owning Panel maxes this across elements to find its hug-width; a wider element (or the screen-edge ceiling) then drives whether this label actually wraps.

    • layoutWithin

      public void layoutWithin(int budget)
      Wrap to the panel-assigned budget. Wrapping is engaged ONLY when the budget is narrower than the text's natural single-line width — at a roomy budget the wrap is cleared so the label reports its intrinsic width (and a later wider pass un-wraps it, reversibly).

      The incoming budget is scaled screen-pixel space (it is compared against the scaled naturalWidth()), but wrapWidth must be a FONT-space number (font.split works on the font's native grid), so the scale is divided back out before storing. The scale is then re-applied at getWidth()/getHeight()/render(RenderContext).

      Parameters:
      budget - horizontal pixels available to this element, in panel content space. Always >= 1.
